nodes.description: HOXD13 is required in the distal limb bud (autopod) for the specification and growth of digit skeletal segments. In BDSD the patterning lesion acts on homologous elements in both hands and feet, shortening or deleting middle phalanges and shortening the fifth metacarpal and metatarsal, and leaving incomplete separation of the second and third toes. No study has examined limb buds carrying the contraction, so this node records the anatomical level at which the lesion acts rather than a measured molecular change.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in HOXD13 underlie syndactyly type V and a novel brachydactyly-syndactyly syndrome.
evidence.snippet: In the family with complex brachydactyly and syndactyly, we detected a deletion of 21 bp in the imperfect GCN (where N denotes A, C, G, or T) triplet-containing exon 1 of HOXD13, which results in a polyalanine contraction of seven residues.

nodes.description: A heterozygous 21 bp deletion in the imperfect GCN triplet repeat of HOXD13 exon 1 removes seven residues from the N-terminal polyalanine tract of the HOXD13 homeodomain transcription factor. This is the opposite change to the seven-or-more alanine expansions that cause synpolydactyly. In cultured cells a seven-alanine-contracted HOXD13 enters the nucleus like the wild type protein, whereas expanded forms are retained in cytoplasmic inclusions, so the cytoplasmic aggregation proposed for the expansion alleles does not explain this allele. Its effect on HOXD13 target-gene regulation has not been measured.
